defects.source_says: EO 13251 is dated December 28, 2001 (EO_13251.txt heading; FR Doc. 02-918, 67 FR 1599), and sec. 4 revokes EO 12343 on issuance. The clause's own judgment reason says the revocation took effect on 2001-12-28. The recorded first_end date is three years before the order existed and contradicts the reasons.

notes: The rationale's phrase '38-clause inventory' describes the machine pieces; the claim itself carries 34 clauses after the documented merges. A correction should state the count consistently.
reasoning: Identity (Dec. 28, 2001, 67 FR 1599, State Department succession) is confirmed. The 34 clauses cover the whole text; the 38 machine pieces were merged, as the inventory overrides explain. EO 13261 sec. 4(i), signed 2002-03-19, replaced sec. 3(b), and the before and after texts are accurately quoted. The OFR notes (Revokes EO 12343; Amended by EO 13261) are addressed. The number search finds only EO 13261, the order itself, and a 2010 notice that cites the number in error. The operative clauses are sound, but the terminated sec. 4 carries a wrong first_end date that is inconsistent with its own reasons, so the claim must be rejected.

notes: The claim does not cite the committee's current continuance. Held EO 14354 (effective Sept. 30, 2025) continues the President's Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities 'until September 30, 2027', which supports the claim's statement that the committee continues on 2026-10-14. The OFR 'Amended by' note on EO 12994 lists EO 13385, but EO 13385 only continues the committee and does not change the text this order amended.
reasoning: Identity (July 25, 2003, 68 FR 44851) confirmed; the 5 clauses cover the whole text. Sec. 5, 'continued until September 30, 2005', ended on its own terms on 2005-09-30, recorded inclusive with the exclusive reading stated; the later continuances are separate commands. Secs. 1-4 are amendments that live in the text of EO 12994. EO 13446 sec. 5, effective 2007-09-30 under its sec. 6, restated EO 12994 and kept the new name, the 'intellectual disabilities' wording and the four added secretaries; the quoted restated text matches the held bytes. The OFR note on EO 13309 ('Amends: EO 12994') is addressed, and the number search finds only the order itself.

notes: Sec. 2(a) is kept operative as to EO 13290 even though the sec. 1 prohibitions it relates to were terminated. The claim discloses this, and no held source ends sec. 2(a).
reasoning: Identity (May 22, 2003, 68 FR 31931) confirmed; the 16 clauses cover the whole text. Sec. 1 (as restated by EO 13364 on 2004-11-29) was terminated by EO 13668 sec. 1 on 2014-05-27; that order has no effective-date clause and states that the emergency 'shall remain in place'. Date, actor, mechanism and quotes are correct. The emergency is continued by 23 held notices, the last of May 4, 2026, which continues it 'for 1 year' beyond May 22, 2026. EO 13315 (effective 2003-08-29) and EO 13350 (effective 2004-07-30) are correctly characterized; EO 13350 does not amend this order's text. The OFR note 'Amended by: EO 13364' is addressed, and the sec. 2(b) savings are accurately described.
